title: Vehicle-agnostic autonomous-systems orchestration layer (the AVO problem: tasking and coordinating heterogeneous multi-vendor uncrewed vehicles across domains)
problem: No fielded, vendor-neutral or government-owned layer can take a commander's intent and task/coordinate heterogeneous uncrewed vehicles from multiple vendors across air, sea and ground domains, so operators run several vendor controllers side by side and DIU/DAWG/Navy are paying a prize challenge to get one.
echelons: Navy unmanned task unit / TF-59-style units
Army brigade/battalion launched-effects and drone cells

user.exact_role: Autonomous-systems mission commander / unmanned task unit watch officer who must task and monitor several vendor fleets at once (with the vehicle operators who run each vendor GCS)
organization_examples: USSOCOM PEO SOF Digital Applications / UxSAI program
Navy unmanned task units (TF-59 lineage, PMS 406 customers)
Army Transformation-in-Contact brigades and launched-effects cells

current_workflow: Each vehicle family arrives with its own vendor ground control station or app (AuterionOS/Mission Control, Kinesis, Shield AI, Lattice, Navy CCS).
Operators run several controllers side by side on separate laptops/tablets; one operator per vehicle family.
Tasks are coordinated verbally, over radio nets or via TAK chat; there is no single intent-to-task interface.
Tracks and status are manually re-entered into the COP, or bridged by a vendor gateway (Lattice SDK, TAK CoT plugin) where one has been integrated.
Engagement approval and airspace deconfliction run in separate fires / C-UAS / airspace systems (FAAD C2, IBCS, TAK airspace apps).
After action, logs are collected per vendor and reconciled by hand for T&E and training.
current_solution: Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy (selected by DIU for Replicator in Nov 2024; SOCOM autonomy integration; Army enterprise agreement), Auterion Nemyx for multi-manufacturer small drones running AuterionOS/Skynode, Shield AI Hivemind for multi-aircraft, and government-owned reference stacks (USAF A-GRA for CCA, SOCOM FANTOM Core, Navy UMAA/CCS) plus TAK as the lowest-common-denominator bridge; the DIU/DAWG/Navy Autonomous Vehicle Orchestrator prize challenge (Jan 2026) is the current attempt to buy a vehicle-agnostic layer.
failure: Vendor lock at the controller: each new vehicle needs a bespoke integration, cross-domain (air-sea-ground) tasking is not vendor-neutral, DDIL behavior differs per stack, and no layer has been accepted that turns intent into coordinated multi-vendor execution; Replicator was dissolved into DAWG without fielding such software and SOCOM says collaborative-autonomy development 'is not moving fast enough'.

evidence.claim: DIU, DAWG and the U.S. Navy launched the Autonomous Vehicle Orchestrator prize challenge on 13 Jan 2026 (max prize pool $100M) seeking vehicle-agnostic software that translates commander intent (voice/text/haptic) into coordinated execution of heterogeneous autonomous fleets; iterative sprints, submissions due 25 Jan 2026, Sprint 1 within 10 days of selection, challenge runs to 31 Dec 2026
evidence.source_title: DIU offers $100M in prizes for voice-controlled AI-enabled drone swarm 'orchestrator' (Breaking Defense) and DIU press release
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The AVO challenge is described as open to U.S.-based technology companies, defense contractors and research organizations with software prototypes approaching production readiness; a $100M prize pool is a ceiling on possible awards, not obligated funds, and no public list of winners beyond reported invitations to SpaceX/xAI (Feb 2026, low-tier source) was found - Public evidence insufficient on awards
evidence.source_title: DIU, DAWG & Navy Launch $100M Prize Challenge for Autonomous Vehicle Orchestrator (ExecutiveGov); SpaceX joins DoD drone swarms orchestrator contest (AI CERTs)
evidence.label: FACT (eligibility) / INFERENCE (participants)

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: INFERENCE

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: It is not that nobody has tried - the best-capitalized new primes (Anduril ~$86M SOCOM, up-to-$20B Army vehicle; Shield AI; Auterion $130M Series B) have attacked exactly this layer, and each has an incentive to make its own stack the orchestrator rather than build a neutral one. Success requires cleared staff, dozens of vehicle integrations whose APIs vendors control, DDIL-hardened distributed engineering, safety cases under DoDD 3000.09 and government trust; the government keeps re-scoping the problem (Replicator to DAWG to the AVO challenge) and simultaneously builds its own kernels (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA) that commoditize the neutral layer a startup would sell. Where partial solutions exist (C-UAS C2, CCA mission autonomy) the government has already picked production vendors.
technical_wedge: Not the orchestrator itself. The only defensible startup-sized wedge is a thin, open protocol-translation and task-allocation kernel (MAVLink / STANAG 4586 / UMAA / CoT / FANTOM-style M2M adapters) with conformance tests, offered to government labs and primes as the reference plumbing under whichever orchestrator wins - but that is a tooling business adjacent to G25, not G25.

mvp.what: Adapter framework plus simple task-allocation engine demonstrating one mission (relay + area search + re-task) across three vehicle stacks (PX4/MAVLink, ArduPilot, a ROS 2 ground robot) in simulation, then live with two Blue UAS airframes, published against public UMAA/STANAG-like interfaces with a conformance test suite.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Simulation-only (Gazebo/AirSim + SITL) heterogeneous mission with intent-to-task allocation and DDIL link-drop behavior; live two-airframe demo only if range access and Blue UAS hardware (~$30-60k) are secured.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That a vendor-neutral layer can task vehicles from three different stacks with deterministic, auditable behavior under link loss, with lower operator load than parallel GCS - and, critically, that a government lab or prime will adopt it, since the AVO challenge itself demands production-approaching prototypes from U.S.-based firms.

data_requirement.what: Vehicle telemetry, mission logs and interface specifications for many vendor stacks; tasking doctrine and CONOPS; datalink and DDIL parameters; later, government reference architecture specs and range data.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Partially: PX4/ArduPilot/MAVLink logs and simulators are open; UMAA design descriptions are partly public via AUVSI; Lattice SDK access requires Anduril partnership; FANTOM Core and A-GRA specs are government-controlled and CUI; realistic CONOPS, threat behaviors and datalink parameters are CUI/ITAR - the non-U.S.-person founder likely cannot receive them without licensing (counsel).
sources: PX4/ArduPilot open-source stacks and SITL logs
Vendor SDKs under partnership (Lattice SDK, AuterionOS)
Government specs (FANTOM Core, A-GRA) only under contract/CUI

integration_requirement.who_controls_the_interface: Platform vendors control their controller APIs (Anduril, Auterion, Shield AI, AV); the government controls the reference kernels (FANTOM Core, A-GRA, UMAA, TAK); a startup controls none of them.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% U.S. citizen or permanent-resident ownership and control; the German founder is expected to become a permanent resident but the Indonesian founder is not assumed to be a U.S. person, so cap-table and control structure need counsel. The AVO challenge is described as open to U.S.-based entities (MEDIUM confidence on exact terms). Autonomy control software for military vehicles is likely ITAR technical data (USML VIII(h)/XI(d)) or EAR 600-series - a non-U.S.-person co-founder would need a DDTC/BIS licence or a technology-control plan to touch the core code; this is a constraint to be structured with export counsel, not a legal conclusion here.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: They do not need to add it - Anduril's Lattice is already the selected orchestration layer for DIU/DAWG, SOCOM and Army C-UAS, Palantir/Anduril hold the NGC2 data layer, and the government's own kernels (FANTOM Core, A-GRA, UMAA) occupy the neutral position. Any startup adapter that gains traction can be absorbed by a Lattice SDK release or a government reference implementation within months.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject for the orchestrator itself. A startup could only win as a neutral, open, government-adoptable kernel - which is precisely what the government is building in-house or buying via the AVO challenge from production-ready U.S. firms; the neutral position has no owner willing to pay a startup for it.

capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: $2M-$5M (3+ real airframes across two domains, range time, DDIL radio testing, one cleared U.S.-person lead, CMMC L2 posture, safety case)
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: $15M-$40M (cleared team, integrations with 5-10 vendor stacks and government kernels, ATO/accreditation, sustained T&E) - and that assumes a program of record chooses a non-incumbent
capital_required.assumptions: Based on S13 capital-intensity assessment and comparable spend by Auterion ($130M Series B, 2025) and Anduril awards; INFERENCE, LOW-MEDIUM confidence.

expertise_required.role: Distributed-systems / autonomy engineer with DDIL consensus and task-allocation experience
expertise_required.why: The hard problem is deterministic multi-vehicle behavior under partition, not UI or MAVLink plumbing

expertise_required.role: Cleared U.S.-person former autonomous-systems operator or program lead (SOCOM/Navy unmanned)
expertise_required.why: Needed to obtain CONOPS, CUI interface specs and a sponsor; required for any classified integration
Orchestration lives or dies on link behavior under EW

expertise_required.role: Safety assurance / T&E specialist (DoDD 3000.09, airworthiness, range safety)
expertise_required.why: Every vehicle integration re-triggers T&E; lethal-effects delegation needs a safety case
ITAR/EAR classification of autonomy software and non-U.S.-person founder structuring

regulatory_burden.explanation: Military multi-vehicle autonomy C2 software is very likely ITAR-controlled technical data (USML VIII(h)/XI(d)) or EAR 600-series once designed for military use; CUI and CMMC Level 2 apply as soon as government interfaces are touched; DoDD 3000.09 policy on autonomy in weapon systems applies to lethal tasking; airworthiness/range approvals for live demos; SECRET-level integration for CCA, Navy fleets and fires. Needs specialist counsel - not a legal judgment.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person likely cannot access ITAR technical data or CUI-marked government interface specs without a licence/technology-control plan, and cannot hold a clearance; the German founder is not a U.S. person until permanent residency is obtained. For this gap the controlled code is the product itself, so the constraint is structural rather than peripheral. Counsel required.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Commercial multi-vendor fleet orchestration exists (inspection, delivery, public safety) but is a thin, price-sensitive market already served by MAVLink fleet-management products (Auterion Mission Control, FlytBase-class tools), and the defense-specific parts (DDIL, lethal tasking, STANAG/UMAA) have no commercial buyer.

defensibility.explanation: Whoever holds many certified vehicle integrations, an ATO and a program-of-record footprint is defensible - which is exactly why Anduril and the government-owned kernels are defensible and a new entrant is not; an open neutral kernel is by design low-moat.

why_now: Replicator (2023) failed to field orchestration software and was dissolved into DAWG (late 2025); the FY27 request ($54.6B) and the Jan 2026 AVO prize challenge show explicit demand for a vehicle-agnostic layer; Drone Dominance is delivering tens of thousands of multi-vendor small drones (12,080 accepted by Sept 2026); open flight stacks, cheap edge compute and mesh radios made multi-manufacturer coordination demonstrable only in late 2025; and government reference architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA) are being asserted against vendor lock. All of this raises demand - but it also means the buyer has already organized its answer around incumbents and government-owned kernels.
killer_risk: The government has already decided who solves this: either Anduril Lattice (selected by DIU, SOCOM and the Army with an enterprise vehicle) or a government-owned kernel (FANTOM Core, A-GRA, UMAA), with the only open door (AVO challenge) restricted to U.S.-based firms with production-approaching prototypes - and the budget that would fund a new entrant was written down from $54.6B to about $1B. A two-student team with $250k and a non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot enter that door, cannot legally hold the core code and cannot safely field DDIL-grade multi-vehicle autonomy.

Replicator announced (Aug 2023) to field thousands of attritable autonomous systems within 18-24 months
DIU selects Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy for Replicator collaborative autonomy (Nov 2024)
SOCOM $86M Anduril autonomy integration (Mar); Auterion Nemyx launch / $130M Series B (Sep); Replicator dissolved into DAWG (late 2025); Auterion multi-manufacturer swarm demo (Dec)

AVO prize challenge launched 13 Jan (submissions due 25 Jan, runs to 31 Dec); Army-Anduril enterprise agreement (Mar); FY27 DAWG request $54.6B (Apr); SOCOM 'not moving fast enough' (May); HASC/SASC mark $1.0B for DAWG (15 Jun); SOCOM ALM notice mandates FANTOM Core (26 Jun); SOCOM UxSAI mission-autonomy T&E (Aug); 12,080 Gauntlet drones accepted (Sep)

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling in principle - AUKUS Maritime Big Play (2025) and the UK Digital Targeting Web show allied demand for common uncrewed-systems C2 interfaces, and European buyers (Bundeswehr, Ukraine) are more open to non-Anduril stacks (Auterion, Helsing, Arondite). But the same structure repeats: allied navies are shaping the software through primes and government labs, Helsing/Auterion/Arondite already occupy the European neutral-orchestration position, and a U.S.-ITAR-tainted product would complicate allied sales. Allies do not rehabilitate G25; they would at most host an adjacent conformance/adapter tooling business.
